items.prompt: For a smooth central first-derivative formula, what cancels to give O(h²)truncation?

options.text: Every odd Taylor term, including the derivative
options.why: That would erase the quantity being estimated.

options.text: The equal even Taylor terms across x+h and x-h
options.why: Subtracting the two expansions leaves the linear term and a cubic remainder before division by2h.

options.text: All function-evaluation noise for every program
The need to stay in the function domain
options.why: Both evaluation points still must be valid.

items.explanation: The central numerator cancels its constant/quadratic terms; third-order remainder divided by h is second order.
